title: Sample 13-5: Poem with Uneven Indention and Wide Spacing

illustrates.quote: Use three blank cells to separate widely spaced words or phrases. Explain the blank cells in a transcriber’s note. Sample: Three blank cells indicate wide spacing. (See Sample 13-5: Poem with Uneven Indention and Wide Spacing on page 13-18.)

blocks.features: Byline, grey italic 'by' + plain name, below the title.

e.e. cummings poem with unevenly indented lines, some words split with wide internal spacing (e.g. 'can  dy  lu' / 'minous', 'greens  coo  l choc' / 'olate'); excerpt ends mid-poem at a torn print edge before 'un  der,'.

print.notes: Picture on PDF p.372; a torn/jagged bottom edge shows the print excerpt cuts off after 's.' and before a further line beginning 'un  der,' -- a genuine excerpt, not the whole poem.
print.printFeatures: Bold title; grey italic 'by'; irregular stepped indention; internal wide word-spacing within several lines.

braille.notes: Verbatim from .txt lines 10781-10801, after stripping a 5-char line-number field (2-digit max line number 21, +3=5) and converting U+2800. Lines 1-2 are the sample's own transcriber's note ('Three blank cells indicate wide spacing.') inside a grade-1 passage, per rule 13.6.3. Title (line 4) is centred; byline (line 6) is centred on its own shorter string. The poem body follows print's uneven indention directly, and the wide-spaced mid-word splits ('can   dy   lu', 'gre5s   coo   ;l *oc') are rendered with three literal blank cells, per this rule. The final '444' line is a continuation marker showing the excerpt is deliberately truncated (matching the source's own torn print edge), not the poem's true ending.

resolution: Run A and run B independently transcribed this item's braille.lines identically, character-for-character; independently re-verified against the cited source .txt lines (U+2800 blank cells / ASCII-space converted, reference-line-number or box-margin field measured and stripped per this section's own convention) as part of this reconciliation. print.blocks content agreed in substance between both runs (only prose-wording differences in `features`/`notes`, not resolved as errors); run A's wording is kept. See compare-gold-13/differences.md for the file-by-file account. CORRECTION during buildModel13 integration: three print.blocks poem lines ('was', 'edible', 'pinks shy') had a lower indent level in run A than run B (2/2/1 vs 3/3/2) -- an A/B disagreement not caught by the braille.lines-only diff, since both runs' braille.lines are byte-identical. Resolved in favour of run B throughout: the gold braille measures 6/6/4 leading cells respectively for these three lines ('      0' for 'was', '      $ible' for 'edible', '    p9ks %y' for 'pinks shy') -- nestedMargins's first=level*2 gives 6/6/4 only at levels 3/3/2, not run A's 2/2/1 (which would give 4/4/2).
